title: Streaming JSON compatibility shim + constrained-decoder canary
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight compatibility shim and accompanying canary harness that validates JSON-mode enforcement and constrained-decoder behaviour across streaming responses and interleaved tool/function calls. This ticket focuses on cross-model compatibility (including quantized variants), partial-stream recovery, and telemetry hooks that let Console show contract adherence per-route. The shim should be opt-in for early experiments and safe to roll back without model changes.
background: We keep seeing intermittent schema drift when streaming responses include tool calls and partial token emissions, particularly on older quantized variants. Existing test suites cover strict parsers, but there is a gap: a deployable shim that (1) normalizes boundary tokens, (2) gates constrained-decoder outputs with a lightweight sentinel strategy, and (3) emits structured telemetry to flag model-specific failure modes. This will let PM/design and infra teams run canaries on real traffic before changing model configs globally.
acceptance_criteria: Shim can be enabled per-route and per-model-version via config flag
Shim normalizes and rewrites common boundary issues (trailing commas, unclosed arrays) for partial streams without changing token-level logits server-side
Constrained-decoder gate rejects obvious schema-violating fragments and emits a repair suggestion token sequence for client-side reassembly
Canary harness runs across 3 model families (base, quantized-int8, int4) and reports pass/fail for 200 golden prompts
Console shows per-route contract-violation rate and a small sample of raw and shimmed outputs
No measurable increase in p99 response latency > 8ms for enabled routes in synthetic load tests
Fallback behavior: if shim fails, requests continue with original decoding path and an incident telemetry event is created
test_plan: 1) Create a golden prompt corpus of 200 prompts that exercise streaming + toolcalls + nested JSON. 2) Run offline compatibility matrix across local runtime builds for target model variants. 3) Deploy canary to 2% of traffic on staging and mirror traffic to experiment cluster. 4) Collect decoder-level telemetry: token acceptance rate, repair attempts, schema-violation tags. 5) Run load tests to confirm latency impact. 6) Run controlled chaos tests where we force partial-stream interruptions and validate recovery heuristics.
implementation_notes:
- Shim runs post-decoder before the stream sink; it is not modifying logits.
- Use a small deterministic patcher that attempts to close truncated JSON structures using minimal token insertions (commas/brackets) and marks repaired regions with sentinel metadata.
- Constrained-decoder gate uses the existing constraint engine but with a tunable threshold to avoid over-blocking.
- Add lightweight sampling to emit both raw and shimmed outputs for first N requests per route for audit.
- Telemetry: contract_violation, repair_attempted, repair_success, shim_activated, shim_error.
risks: Shim may mask model regressions by auto-repairing outputs instead of surfacing them
Increased observability cost due to emitting both raw and repaired payloads for audit
Edge cases where repair inserts change meaning and create downstream data integrity issues
Potential compatibility differences across quantized kernels leading to false positives in canary
mitigations: Limit repair attempts to non-destructive fixes (closing brackets, adding commas) and never mutate scalar values
Require sampling of raw outputs to be stored for at least 7 days to support audits
Add manual review step in Console to approve any automated repair rules before wide rollout
Run canaries concurrently on model variants and fail fast if variant-specific error spikes appear
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature branch + unit tests (2 weeks). Phase 2: Offline matrix runs + staging canary (1 week). Phase 3: Gradual staging traffic canary 1% -> 5% with monitoring (3 days). Phase 4: Rollout to production 0.5% -> 5% over 48 hours with automated rollback triggers on violation rate > 0.5% or p99 latency regression > 8ms. Finalize with a postmortem and decision on making shim default for select routes.
notes: PM wants experiment results before EOW. Prioritize building the golden corpus and telemetry hooks first.
Design reviewed the repair UI; need one more session to agree on sentinel display in Console.
We should coordinate with Platform to ensure canary clusters have identical kernel builds for fairness testing.
